newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court orders halt to work on power plant.
newsitem.headline: French court orders halt to work on power plant.

text.p: A French court on Tuesday ordered suspension of work on a new power plant near the mouth of the Loire river in a victory for environmentalists.

The court in the western city of Nantes ruled that the ecological impact of the planned power station at Le Carnet had not been adequately studied. It suspended a permit allowing state utility Electricite de France (EDF) to do preliminary earth-moving work.
The court said further study was needed to decide if the plant, on wetlands in the Loire estuary, should be built or not.

Five environmental groups including the World Wide Fund for Nature had sought the court order to bar construction of the power station, already approved by Prime Minister Alain Juppe's government, saying it threatened wildlife.
EDF has yet to decide if the plant will be nuclear-powered or fired by fossil fuel. France generates about 75 percent of its electricity from nuclear power, one of the highest rates in the world.
Ecologists hailed Tuesday's ruling but urged further action to scrap the plant. Thousands of people have attended rallies against the planned power station, about 40 km (25 miles) from Nantes.
